title: Pokémon Battle Clone
tagline: A turn-based battle system built to show how a rule-heavy game can live in a pure, fully tested domain layer, now with online 1v1.
overview: A recreation of the Pokémon battle system focused on **rules and architecture, not visual polish**. The battle logic lives in a domain layer that knows nothing about Unity, so it can be tested, reused and extended without touching the engine.
It supports the full turn loop, move effects with probabilities, and **online two-player battles**.

highlights.title: Full turn flow
highlights.text: Action selection, priority, switching Pokémon and move execution, with the battle state managed end to end.

highlights.title: Moves with real rules
highlights.text: Damage, stat stages, healing and recoil, plus accuracy checks and secondary effects that trigger with a probability.

highlights.title: Online multiplayer
highlights.text: Two players battle through a 6-character lobby code, with handling for the rival disconnecting.

highlights.title: Deterministic and testable
highlights.text: A fixed seed makes a battle reproducible, which is what makes the probabilistic parts testable.

decisions.title: Four layers, one direction of dependency
decisions.text: **Domain** (battle rules), **Application** (orchestrates the flow), **Infrastructure** (data loading, integrations) and **Presentation** (Unity-specific UI). The domain never references the engine.

decisions.title: Turns as an async flow
decisions.text: Each turn runs in three phases (start, action selection, execution) implemented with `async/await`, so waiting for a player, an AI or a remote client looks the same to the battle.

decisions.title: Battle events drive the visuals
decisions.text: Every action emits events (damage, stat change, miss, immunity, fainted) that are processed in sequence and move both the animations and the battle log. The domain never calls the UI.

decisions.title: Trainers are interchangeable strategies
decisions.text: `PlayerTrainer`, `RivalTrainer` and `NetworkTrainer` share the same `ITrainerStrategy`. Deciding an action is separated from executing it.

decisions.title: Network layer decoupled from the domain
decisions.text: Built on **Photon Fusion 2 (Shared Mode)**. Both clients run the same battle with a shared seed and only exchange actions as small DTOs over RPC. The `NetworkTrainer` simply awaits the remote action with a `TaskCompletionSource`.

decisions.title: Injected randomness
decisions.text: RNG goes through an `IRandom` interface, so tests and online clients can replay exactly the same battle.

decisions.title: Data-driven moves
decisions.text: A move is a main effect plus optional extra effects with a probability, configured without code changes. Content is imported from PokeAPI with a custom editor tool ([PokeTool](#poketool)).

limitations: Status conditions, abilities, weather and critical hits are not implemented yet.
learnings: Modeling a rule-heavy system with many interacting mechanics so that new moves and effects don't require changing existing code.
Testing probabilistic behavior by controlling the source of randomness instead of fighting it.
Keeping networking out of the domain: the network is just another way of deciding an action.
